description:
Investigation of an OOM crash on a FreeBSD instance using fetcher.cr identified several real memory-safety issues. This epic tracks the fixes.

Background: A user reported OOM kills on FreeBSD specifically (not seen on Linux). FreeBSD's jemalloc + larger default fiber stacks amplify issues that are latent on Linux. The crashes correlate with parsing large RSS/JSON feeds.

Root causes:
1. `XMLStreamingParser#check_xxe_risk` reads the ENTIRE remaining stream into memory for non-seekable IO, then allocates a duplicate buffer. 2x peak memory, no size cap.
2. DOM parsers (`RSSParser#parse_xml`, software providers' JSON parsing) build full AST with no body-size enforcement.
3. Streaming parser's `parse_entries` skips the memory limit that `parse_complete` enforces.
4. Two P0/P1 tickets (`fetcherc-kw8`, `fetcherc-jzl`) were closed without the underlying bugs actually being fixed. They are being reopened as part of this work.

Targets a 0.9.24 patch release.
title: [EPIC] 0.9.24 OOM fixes for FreeBSD
